role: The first corpus in this repository that reproduces Telegraph's own measurement. Registration 506's binary scores +0.1996 here against the 0.1929 Telegraph reported for it, a difference of 0.007, where the near-miss corpus put the same binary at +0.6055 and our own intent corpus at +0.6055 as well. Telegraph described their fixture as exercising 'the core discrimination paths for this intent', and this is what that appears to mean: the good answer is a fluent paraphrase of the ground truth, the bad answer is a fluent sentence that is plainly wrong. No near-misses, no edge cases.
how_to_read_it: Average separation is the mean of score(good) minus score(bad) across all pairs, which is Telegraph's definition, with cases excluded rather than zeroed when either module fails to score. The champion bar was 0.4941 at registration 506 and moves whenever a new champion is promoted.
what_it_shows: Our correct answers are the problem, not our wrong ones. Average correct-answer score is 0.5045 against an average wrong-answer score of 0.2628. A fluent correct paraphrase scores 0.2479 on the wind case and 0.2866 on the temperature case, and three pairs tie exactly because correct and wrong land on the same clamp. Our anchor and ambiguity rules fire on the GOOD answer, because a paraphrase by construction does not repeat the ground truth's wording. If correct paraphrases scored 0.90 with wrong answers untouched, average separation would be +0.6372.
